questions.stem: Why does a dimension table in a star schema usually get its own surrogate key instead of using the source system's key?

options.text: A surrogate key stays stable when source keys change or collide, and it lets one business key have several historical versions
A surrogate key removes the need to load the fact table
Surrogate keys are required before a table can be stored as Delta
Surrogate keys make the source system's updates faster

questions.explanation: A surrogate key is assigned by the warehouse, so it doesn't change when a source system reuses or renumbers keys, keys from two sources can't collide, and a slowly changing dimension can keep several rows for one business key, each with its own surrogate key.

questions.stem: A customer moves from Leeds to York. Reports must show past sales under Leeds and new sales under York. How should the Customer dimension handle the change?

options.text: Add a new row for the customer with a new surrogate key and the new city, and mark the old row as no longer current
Delete the customer and their sales, then reload them
Add a CurrentCity column and keep the old city in the original column
Overwrite the city on the existing row

questions.explanation: Keeping history this way is a type 2 slowly changing dimension: the old row keeps the old city and stays linked to past facts, and new facts use the new row's surrogate key. Overwriting (type 1) loses history, and an extra column (type 3) keeps only one previous value.

questions.stem: Which two columns does a type 2 slowly changing dimension typically add to each row? Each correct answer is part of the solution.

options.text: A foreign key to the fact table
The date the row version stopped being valid, or a flag for the current row
A copy of the fact table's measures
The name of the pipeline that loaded the row
The date the row version became valid

questions.explanation: Start and end dates (or a current-row flag) say which version of a member was true at a point in time, so facts can be matched to the right version. Dimensions don't hold foreign keys to facts or copies of their measures; facts point to dimensions.

questions.stem: Put the steps of a nightly dimensional load in order.

options.text: Land the changed source rows in staging tables
Look up each fact row's dimension surrogate keys
Insert the fact rows
Insert new dimension members and apply changes to existing ones

questions.explanation: Dimensions are loaded before facts so every fact row can find its dimension members' surrogate keys. Loading facts first would leave rows pointing at members that don't exist yet.

questions.stem: A Product dimension gets its surrogate keys from an automatically generated column. A developer suggests truncating and fully reloading the dimension every night to keep the code simple. Why is this a bad idea?

options.text: Surrogate keys can't be generated again once the table has been truncated
A full reload always takes longer than an SCD type 1 update of every row
TRUNCATE TABLE isn't supported on dimension tables in a Fabric warehouse
The reload would give members new keys and invalidate the keys already stored in fact tables

questions.explanation: Truncating and reloading a dimension with generated surrogate keys invalidates the fact data that references them, and SCD type 2 history might not be rebuildable. TRUNCATE is supported (it's recommended for staging tables).

questions.stem: A Customer dimension keeps SCD type 2 history. When the fact load looks up the customer's surrogate key for a new sale, which row should it use?

options.text: The current version of the customer
The version with the highest surrogate key whatever its current flag
Any version, because all versions share the same surrogate key
The first version ever inserted for the customer

questions.explanation: For an SCD type 2 dimension, the fact load retrieves the surrogate key of the current version. Versions have different surrogate keys, because the natural key repeats across versions.

questions.stem: You're building a Date dimension. How should its surrogate key be stored?

options.text: As an IDENTITY integer that starts at 1 for the earliest date
As a date value equal to the natural key
As an int in YYYYMMDD format, for example 20250406
As a string in DD/MM/YYYY format

questions.explanation: The guidance is a YYYYMMDD int surrogate key: compact, sorted numerically and ISO 8601 conformant. The date data type is for the natural key, and an IDENTITY key would give the key no meaning, which date keys are the exception to.

questions.stem: A product was discontinued and removed from the source system, but past sales still reference it. What should the dimension load do?

options.text: Delete the product row and its fact rows together
Insert a new SCD type 2 version with blank attributes
Mark the product as a soft delete so that it's no longer active
Delete the product row so that the dimension matches the source

questions.explanation: Source deletions shouldn't be synchronized to the dimension; record them as soft deletes and filter them out in reports. Hard deletes break facts that reference the member, and an SCD version with blank attributes isn't a deletion.

questions.stem: Sales facts carry several small, low-cardinality attributes: IsGift, OrderStatus and PaymentType. You want them out of the fact table without creating three tiny dimensions. What should you create?

options.text: A junk dimension that stores the combinations of these values with a surrogate key
A degenerate dimension for each attribute inside the fact table
A role-playing dimension that the fact table references three times
A snowflake dimension with one normalized table per attribute

questions.explanation: A junk dimension consolidates many small, low-cardinality dimensions such as flags and status values into one table. A degenerate dimension is something like an order number at fact grain, and role-playing reuses one dimension in several roles.

questions.stem: A customer's tracked attribute changes in a dimension that applies SCD type 2. Which two actions should the dimension load take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.

options.text: Insert a new row whose start date equals that end date and whose current flag is TRUE
Update the changed attribute on the current row and keep its current flag TRUE
Delete the current row and insert the new values under the same surrogate key
Set the new row's end date to the ETL processing date and its current flag to FALSE
Set the current row's end date to the ETL processing date and its current flag to FALSE

questions.explanation: SCD type 2 expires the existing version and inserts a new current version. Updating in place is SCD type 1, and reusing the surrogate key or expiring the new row breaks the history.
